| Scene description | • The site is at the interface of paths and water in Zhongshan Park, Jianghan District.<br>• S15-B-01 shows an overflowing black square bin at a wooden boardwalk edge, with exposed bags, cardboard and foam meal containers. Pebble paving, a grey path, still water and moored boats surround it.<br>• S15-B-02 shows a pair of non-overflowing bins labelled ‘Zhongshan Park’, ‘Recyclables’ and ‘Residual waste’ beside planting. A bulging black bag in planting to the left suggests accumulation; dry leaves, trees and small buildings appear nearby. No targets were detected in the remaining images, which were not supplied and are not described. |
| Regulatory basis | • Park managers should collect waste and maintain bins daily, prevent spills and accumulation, and keep surroundings clean. Regulations on Urban Appearance and Environmental Sanitation Management, Article 32.<br>• Littering or stockpiling in public areas and dumping, scattering or stockpiling outside designated locations are prohibited. Regulations on Urban Appearance and Environmental Sanitation Management, Article 26.<br>• Containers should be appropriately placed and clearly labelled, with compliant signs for effective classification. Signs for classification of municipal solid waste (GB/T 19095-2019), Section 4.1.<br>• Overflow or accumulation left uncleared for over 24 hours constitutes poor management, requiring time-limited correction and potentially fines where collection or management duties are unfulfilled. Regulations on Urban Appearance and Environmental Sanitation Management, Article 36.<br>• Park collection points should be accessible in busy areas and checked regularly to prevent accumulation or overflow. Code for the Design of Public Parks (GB 51192-2016), Section 7.3.5. |
| Severity | Moderate. One overflowing bin and one planted-area accumulation violate basic sanitation requirements without extensive pollution or sanitation hazards. Their location beside paths and water may prompt complaints and affect the park’s image. |
| Impact assessment | Visible effects: exposed waste in S15-B-01 impairs appearance and may attract insects and rodents; the bulging S15-B-02 bag presents odour and pathogen risks. Near-term risks: wind may spread waste onto paths or water, particularly under cloudy conditions with force 2–3 winds, and cause complaints or poorer sanitation assessments. |
| Potential causes | • Delayed collection may cause overflow: S15-B-01 exposes waste without signs of removal.<br>• Visitors or staff may dispose improperly: the S15-B-02 bag lies outside bins among leaves, suggesting it was not left by collection work.<br>• Verify collection and check logs and compare collection frequency with generation to assess delays. |
| Long-term effects | Persistent or recurrent problems could worsen sanitation and satisfaction, lead to adverse environmental assessments, and pollute nearby water, affecting ecological safety. |
| Recommendations | • Immediate action: empty S15-B-01, remove the S15-B-02 bag, disinfect bins and check nearby containers for impending overflow.<br>• Longer-term action: check bins every 4 hours, add temporary collection points in busy areas, promote classification, and maintain traceable collection records. |
| Priority | Medium. Overflow and accumulation affect the park and visitors without major pollution or public-safety risk. Their waterside location presents spread risks. Complete clearance and correction within 24 hours. |
